what_it_is: The board scene of record — and honest about what it is: a 2026-10-24 BACKFILL (JOB BOARD-SCENES-BACKFILL), built because the piece predates the HTML-SCENE LAW and the board could only offer a YouTube embed Hadi's phone walled with a bot check (his Action #34). The scene reconstructs the published piece from its own production data — hidden_files/ws01/S/: its timeline.json (line windows) and word_events.json (323 measured word times) — and from frames sampled from the published render itself, because the piece's visuals are code-drawn animation (scenes_single.py) with no static plates to reuse. The MP4 was NOT re-rendered from this scene; the scene plays the production file's own material. The registry, the board links and this package name this file as the piece's scene of record.
in_scene_records: The scene carries a decision block in-page: <script type="application/json" id="decisions"> — 4 records with a coverage header (4/4 elements recorded, undecided []): DR-BACKFILL (the scene itself: rebuilt from the piece's production data; faithful, not modernized — same images, same words, same order, same timings as the published video), DR-SCRIPT (the locked script: one arc per QC T-15; the H and W delivery-form builds named as the alternatives, the single being the published form), DR-VISUALS (code-drawn diagram states; in this scene the plates are frames of the published render sampled at line starts and every ~2.6 s within a line, crossfaded — with its own flagged caveat, quoted in plan_and_plates below), DR-AUDIO (the published MP4's own audio track, re-encoded to MP3 192k — the exact mix viewers heard). These are scene-construction records — the backfill's account of itself — and they live here, in this file's provenance; they are NOT the piece's element inventory (decisions/decisions.json carries the 2026-10-23 context audit's 16 elements) and contain no per-word decisions. There is NO word-decision container in this scene (grep-verified at this migration).
plan_and_plates: The scene's plan (the D object): total 106.624 s (the scene's clock; the render's container duration is 106.700 s), contentEnd 99.914 s, 12 phrases (one per line) holding 323 word objects — each a start time + display parameters (cx, cy, size, key, col, shadow), NO end times and NO treatment decisions (see decisions/word-decisions.json). 54 plates: frames of the piece's own finished render sampled at line starts and within lines (the plan's notes name each plate's sample time). DR-VISUALS' flagged caveat, carried as written: 'between samples, motion is a crossfade, not the render's continuous animation. Words, order, timings, narration and every diagram state at sample points are the published piece's own.' The published render's own text layer is block-reveal caption blocks (upload package: V-14 PASS, block-reveal confirmed by pixel measurement) — the context audit's standing note for this piece: 'Published before V-16: caption blocks are a known standards debt vs the current word-animation law, not an undocumented choice.' The scene's per-word objects are the backfill's presentation of the build's measured word times, not a claim that the published build animated per word.
audio_embedded: The scene embeds the published programme audio (one data:audio stream: MP3, 48 kHz, stereo, 106.624 s, 2,560,468 B, sha256 32276fb1ee6eab071a6551e9b9a5c122ac973560d30400084fb3dabf14b13d0f — extracted and measured at this migration): the published MP4's own mix (guide narration + bed, container intro/outro included), re-encoded to MP3 192k per the scene's DR-AUDIO record. The clone upgrade is Tier B and no candidate exists, so no swapped voice exists anywhere for this piece — the scene's embedded audio and the render's audio are the same guide programme in two encodes.

board_edition.note: The board-served edition's bytes DIFFER from the master scene file above (hashes recorded side by side; no identity is claimed). The package carries the master scene of record — the file the registry, the kit and the board links name as the piece's scene.

scene_decomposition.note: The scene ships as one self-contained file, as delivered. Decomposing it into separate HTML/CSS/JS files is a future, separately recorded decision (metadata field scene_decomposition).
